title: Support playbook: troubleshoot SDK retries, timeouts, and streaming disconnects (request_id-first)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
## Context
Support and oncall triage has been slowed by inconsistent SDK behavior and inconsistent information collected from customers (missing request_id, unclear timeout settings, “it works in TS but not Python”). As part of the SDK parity rollout, we need a standard support playbook that is:
- request_id-first
- consistent across Python/TypeScript/Go
- explicit about retry/timeout defaults + how customers can tune them safely
- clear about streaming-specific failure modes (proxy disconnects, partial output, non-idempotent retries)

This ticket creates/updates support troubleshooting guidance and ensures it is linked from the existing Confluence “top support drivers” page.

## Goals / Deliverables
1) Publish a support playbook page (Confluence) covering:
   - What to ask for in the first response (SDK version, language, request_id, timestamps, region, streaming vs non-streaming, config)
   - How to diagnose: 429s, timeouts, 5xx/network errors, and streaming disconnects
   - How to safely recommend changes (timeouts, retry attempts, backoff) and what NOT to recommend (blind retries for streaming)
   - When to escalate to SRE/platform and what artifacts to attach
2) Update support macros / internal notes to standardize intake questions.
3) Add links from: `sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues/sdk-inconsistencies-top-support-drivers.json` to the playbook.

## Where this lives
- Primary: Confluence support runbook under DevEx / Support (linked from “SDK inconsistencies: top support drivers”).
- Secondary: snippet to paste into Zendesk/Helpdesk macros (short checklist).

## Playbook: Intake Checklist (first reply)
Ask customers to provide:
- **SDK language + version** (e.g., redwood-sdk-python 1.x, redwood-sdk-typescript 2.x, redwood-sdk-go 0.x)
- **Endpoint + mode**: chat/text/embeddings; streaming vs non-streaming
- **Timestamp + timezone** and approximate duration of incident
- **Request IDs**:
  - Prefer the server-issued **request_id** from the SDK error object/logging hook
  - If multiple retries happened, ask for **all request_ids** (or confirm whether request_id changed per attempt)
- **HTTP status code + error code** (if available)
- **Retry/timeout configuration** (explicit config + whether they rely on env vars)
- **Network context**: behind proxy, corporate TLS inspection, VPC egress, serverless runtime limits
- **Sample minimal repro** (sanitized), including whether they can reproduce on a different network

Important: instruct customers **not to send API keys** and to redact Authorization headers from logs.

## Quick classification guide
### A) 429 / rate limiting
Signals:
- HTTP 429; may include `Retry-After`
- Customer may see bursty failures or “retry storm” symptoms

What to do:
- Confirm whether they are using SDK defaults or custom retry.
- Ask for `Retry-After` value if present.
- Ask for concurrency settings / parallelism; check if they increased retries + attempts.
- Recommend:
  - Respect `Retry-After` (standard SDK behavior in parity versions)
  - Reduce concurrency or add client-side queueing
  - If they need higher throughput: discuss Dedicated capacity / quota adjustments (route to CSM/AE)

Escalate to platform if:
- 429 responses lack `Retry-After` for the affected endpoint/region (request_id required)
- Error codes are inconsistent across endpoints for the same policy condition

### B) Timeouts (connect/read/overall)
Signals:
- “timeout” errors without HTTP status; or partial response then timeout
- For streaming: “stream disconnected” / EOF mid-chunk

What to do:
- Clarify **which timeout** is being hit:
  - connect timeout (cannot establish connection)
  - overall/request timeout
  - streaming idle/read timeout (no bytes for N seconds)
- Confirm runtime constraints (serverless max execution time, mobile background limits).

Safe recommendations:
- Increase **overall timeout** for long generations.
- For streaming behind proxies, consider a higher **idle/read timeout** to tolerate buffering.
- If timeouts appear “ignored” in streaming, ask for SDK version and confirm they’re on the parity release line.

Escalate to SDK owners if:
- Customer is on the parity release and still sees configured timeouts not honored (attach repro + versions)
- Error object lacks request_id or timeout type

### C) 5xx / transient network errors
Signals:
- 500/502/503/504
- connection resets, DNS failures, TLS handshake issues

What to do:
- Confirm whether errors are intermittent and whether retries improve outcome.
- Ask if failures cluster by region.
- Ask for request_id(s) and exact exception messages.

Safe recommendations:
- Keep retries enabled for 5xx and common network errors.
- Avoid large max_attempts in high-QPS workloads (risk: amplify incident).

Escalate to SRE if:
- Elevated 5xx correlated across customers/regions
- Suspected retry amplification during incident (provide retry_count, timestamps, request volumes)

### D) Streaming disconnects / partial output
Signals:
- Customer receives partial tokens then disconnect
- Often occurs behind corporate proxies (buffering/idle timeouts)

What to do:
- Confirm streaming transport details: browser fetch/EventSource vs server-side, proxy presence.
- Ask whether disconnect happens at a consistent time threshold (proxy idle timeout pattern).
- Ask if they receive partial output and if they can log it.

Guidance to provide:
- **Do not automatically retry streaming** unless they have an idempotency strategy.
- If they need retry semantics, recommend:
  - use non-streaming for idempotent retries, OR
  - implement app-level idempotency keys and “resume” logic (where feasible), OR
  - retry only before any tokens are received (best-effort; still may duplicate billing depending on where disconnect occurred)
- Encourage logging: request_id, retry_count, and streaming_disconnect_reason (if available in their SDK version).

Escalate if:
- Streaming errors lack request_id
- Disconnection reason suggests server-side termination without corresponding status

## Standard artifacts to attach on escalation
- request_id(s)
- SDK name + version
- region + endpoint path
- whether streaming
- retry configuration (max_attempts, backoff, respect_retry_after)
- timeout configuration (overall/connect/read/idle)
- sanitized logs showing retry_count and error codes

## Macro text (short)
“Please share: (1) SDK + version, (2) streaming or non-streaming, (3) timestamps + timezone, (4) request_id(s) from the error/logs, (5) HTTP status + error code, (6) your retry + timeout config, (7) whether you’re behind a corporate proxy/VPN. Please redact all API keys/Authorization headers.”

## Links (internal)
- Top support drivers page to update/link from:
  - `sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues/sdk-inconsistencies-top-support-drivers.json`
- Retry/timeout standard:
  - `sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/sdk-retry-timeout-standard.json`
- Migration notes (for support to reference when asking customers to upgrade):
  - `sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/sdk-migration-notes-auth-retry-timeout.json`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Confluence playbook page published and visible to Support + Eng Oncall
- [x] Linked from “SDK inconsistencies: top support drivers” page
- [x] Support macro/checklist drafted and shared in #support
- [x] Guidance aligns with ADRs on retry + timeout + streaming limitations

## Rollout notes
- Announce in #support and #eng-oncall; ask support to request request_id in the first reply for all SDK-related tickets.
- After 2 weeks, review: % of tickets with request_id included in first response; time-to-triage for SDK issues; number of “need more info” loops.
